title: Recording contract: exact witness data and leading-order witness geometry

key_results.statement: For the recording contract $C=\sum_h\lvert h\rangle\langle h\rvert\otimes K_h$: $e^{-\mathrm{i}C\lambda}=\sum_h\lvert h\rangle\langle h\rvert\otimes e^{-\mathrm{i}K_h\lambda}$.
$p_h(\lambda)=\lvert\phi_h\rvert^2$ for every $\lambda\ge0$ (independent of $\lambda$), and $H_V=H_{T(a)}$: every place of $a$ occurs, because $\phi_h\neq0$ for every $h$.

The branch states are the unit vectors $\lvert E_h(\lambda)\rangle=e^{-\mathrm{i}K_h\lambda}\lvert\chi\rangle$ with amplitudes $a_h=\phi_h$, and $\varrho_h(\lambda)=e^{-\mathrm{i}K_h\lambda}\lvert\chi\rangle\langle\chi\rvert e^{\mathrm{i}K_h\lambda}$.
$W(h,h';\lambda)=\bigl\lvert\langle\chi\rvert e^{\mathrm{i}K_{h'}\lambda}e^{-\mathrm{i}K_h\lambda}\lvert\chi\rangle\bigr\rvert^2$, exactly for all $\lambda\ge0$ and independent of $\phi$.
$\operatorname{Var}_\chi(K_h-K_{h'})=\lVert u_h-u_{h'}\rVert^2$, with the record vectors $\lvert u_h\rangle=(K_h-\langle K_h\rangle)\lvert\chi\rangle$.

With $g(v,w)=\operatorname{Re}\langle v\vert w\rangle$ on $\mathcal H_c$ and $h\sim_0h'$ iff $u_h=u_{h'}$: $(H_V/{\sim_0},d_0)$ is isometric to the configuration $\{u_h\}$ with the Euclidean distance of $(\mathcal H_c,g)$.
$\langle\chi\vert u_h\rangle=0$ for every $h$, so every record vector lies in the orthogonal complement $\chi^\perp$ of $\lvert\chi\rangle$ (real dimension $2d_c-2$).

The leading-order dimension $\dim_0:=\dim_{\mathbb R}\operatorname{aff}_{\mathbb R}\{u_h\}$ satisfies $\dim_0\le\min(d_{T(a)}-1,\,2d_c-2)$, with $d_{T(a)}$ the number of places of $a$; the bound is attained for suitable $K_h$.

Line: $W(h_i,h_j;\lambda)=F\bigl((i-j)\lambda\bigr)$ exactly for all $\lambda\ge0$, with $F(s)=\lvert\langle\chi\rvert e^{-\mathrm{i}sX}\lvert\chi\rangle\rvert^2$ even, so $W$ depends on $i,j,\lambda$ only through $\lvert i-j\rvert\lambda$.

Plane, $K_{h_{(i,j)}}=iX+jY$: $d_0\bigl(h_{(i,j)},h_{(i',j')}\bigr)=\sqrt{\sigma_X^2(\Delta i)^2+2\operatorname{Cov}_\chi(X,Y)\,\Delta i\,\Delta j+\sigma_Y^2(\Delta j)^2}$, with $\Delta i=i-i'$, $\Delta j=j-j'$ and $\operatorname{Cov}_\chi(X,Y)=\operatorname{Re}\langle u_X\vert u_Y\rangle$.
Plane ($n\ge2$): $d_0=\sigma\sqrt{(\Delta i)^2+(\Delta j)^2}$ for all pairs with some $\sigma>0$ (Euclidean square lattice) iff $\sigma_X=\sigma_Y=\sigma>0$ and $\operatorname{Cov}_\chi(X,Y)=0$.

definitions.name: Controlled operators of the recording contract

open_issues: d_0(h,h') = 0 gives only 1 − W = o(λ²); it does not imply h ≈ h' at λ > 0 when K_h and K_h' do not commute, and W = 1 at isolated λ (revivals) does not imply d_0 = 0, so ∼_0 and ≈ at finite λ are different identifications; their relation at finite λ is out of scope.
In the plane example the exact finite-λ form of W is not derived: it depends only on (Δi·λ, Δj·λ) when [X,Y] = 0, by the argument for the line, but in general not otherwise; large λ is out of scope.

consistency_checks.check: λ = 0: the state is the product |φ⟩⊗|χ⟩ and W(h,h';0) = 1 for all pairs, so all places are ≈-equivalent and X_V is a single point.
All K_h equal to K: W ≡ 1 by the exact formula, all u_h are equal, so d_0 ≡ 0 and dim_0 = 0, consistent with the expansion at zero variance.
|χ⟩ an eigenvector of every K_h: the branch states differ only by phases, so W ≡ 1 and u_h = 0, consistent with the criterion (5.12) and the orthogonality (5.13).
